The Gaels, led by first-year head coach [[Rick Pitino]], played their home games at the [[Hynes Athletic Center]] in [[New Rochelle, New York]] as members of the [[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference]]. In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], they finished the season 12–6, 6–3 in [[2020–21 Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference men's basketball season|MAAC play]] to finish in a tie for ninth place. As the No. 9 seed in the [[2021 MAAC men's basketball tournament|MAAC tournament]], they defeated [[Quinnipiac Bobcats men's basketball|Quinnipiac]], Siena, and Niagara to advance to the tournament championship game. They defeated [[2020–21 Fairfield Stags men's basketball team|Fairfield]] to win the tournament championship and earned the conference's automatic bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. They received a No. 15 seed in the East region and lost in the first round to No. 2 seed [[2020–21 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] 68–55.{{Cite web|title=Iona vs. Alabama – Game Recap – March 20, 2021 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401310915|access-date=2021-08-24|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} The Gaels marked the fifth team Pitino had taken to the NCAA Tournament, tying him with [[Lon Kruger]] and [[Tubby Smith]], for the record for most teams taken to the tournament.{{Cite web|last=Gleeson|first=Scott|title=Rick Pitino is back in the NCAA Tournament – with the Iona Gaels|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/03/13/rick-pitino-back-ncaa-tournament-mid-major-team/4684332001/|access-date=2021-08-24|website=USA TODAY|language=en-US}} ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Iona Gaels men's basketball team|Gaels]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 12–17, 9–11 in MAAC play to finish in a tie for sixth place.
